rows.Blog Title: How to Turn Meeting Notes into Tasks Your Team Actually Completes
rows.Key Points: Capture transcript or notes; extract action items with source context; review task drafts before adding to board; assign an owner and clear outcome; check priorities and follow up; Taskwise suggested tasks require human review. Never imply every task is automatically committed.
rows.Subheading: A practical workflow from meeting memory to reviewed action.
rows.Summary: Convert meeting notes into clear tasks with owners, context and a repeatable review step.

rows.Blog Title: Why AI Meeting Tasks Need a Human Review Step
rows.Key Points: Distinguish suggestion from confirmed commitment; detect duplicate/noisy task drafts; verify original meeting context; correct scope, owners and due dates; avoid inventing promises; Taskwise review before board lifecycle; acknowledge judgment limits.
rows.Subheading: Keep useful automation while preserving team judgment.
rows.Summary: A review checklist that turns AI suggestions into trustworthy action items.

rows.Blog Title: Give AI Agents Useful Meeting Context with Taskwise MCP
rows.Key Points: Explain workspace-scoped meeting memory and task tools; distinction read/write permissions; use API keys carefully; ask grounded questions tied to sources; verify proposed actions; audit operations; avoid guarantees about external agents and do not publish real keys.
rows.Subheading: Connect agents to the context your team already captured.
rows.Summary: Use scoped MCP access to connect meeting memory and tasks to an agent workflow.

rows.Blog Title: From Fathom Recording to Reviewed Follow-up Tasks
rows.Key Points: Connect existing Fathom capture; inspect transcript after import; separate decisions from suggestions; review drafts; assign follow-up; monitor sync/duplicates; mention supported integration only, no invented real-time SLA or undocumented trigger setup.
rows.Subheading: Use meeting capture as the start of an execution routine.
rows.Summary: A practical Fathom-to-Taskwise workflow for reviewing and following up on meeting actions.

rows.Blog Title: How to Prioritize Action Items After a Busy Week of Meetings
rows.Key Points: Gather reviewed actions; distinguish urgency, dependencies and importance; use deterministic prioritization and planning workspace; cap work in progress; clarify owners; revisit stale commitments; avoid claims AI magically knows priorities.
rows.Subheading: Make a realistic plan from competing meeting commitments.
rows.Summary: A simple framework for choosing the next useful action after multiple meetings.

rows.Blog Title: The Meeting Follow-up Checklist: Context, Owner, Outcome and Reminder
rows.Key Points: Document the decision; attach source context; define actionable outcome; assign single accountable owner; review before board; decide timing and dependency; use connected follow-up tools where supported; close feedback loop. No invented automatic message behavior.
rows.Subheading: A repeatable checklist for stronger meeting follow-through.
rows.Summary: Seven practical checks that keep meeting commitments visible and actionable.
